title: Countable linear orders of exact Sigma_(lambda+2) Scott-sentence complexity at every nonzero limit lambda

context_spans.label: initial and final segments of lexicographic Z powers

standard_prerequisites.name: Standard infinitary Scott analysis
standard_prerequisites.statement: Orbit-definability/Scott-sentence complexity criteria, interval back-and-forth, and the equality of parameterized rank with the maximum ranks of intervals separated by named points.

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical scattered-order rank bounds
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a scattered order of bounded Hausdorff rank, the standard Alvir-Rossegger/Ash Scott bounds; a parameter-definable interval cannot exceed the ambient Scott rank. Source-specific Z-power comparison and marker construction are provided in full.

core_obligations: Build an order with marker blocks and cofinally increasing Z-power intervals, together with bounded-rank approximants that agree farther and farther in back-and-forth rank.
Place these approximants along a distinguished cofinal sequence in a dense order, and define all parameterized tuple orbits below lambda using marker positions and the approximation indices.

Compare the two nonautomorphic distinguished points by a lambda+1 back-and-forth strategy based on eventual approximation agreement, obtaining the strict lower bound beyond the parameterized upper bound.
difficulty_reason: Unlike the prepared lambda+3 shuffle construction, this result builds a nonuniform cofinal approximation pattern and distinguishes its cut at rank lambda+1. Both the parameterized orbit descriptions and the matching lower-bound strategy remain substantial after the standard scattered-order inputs.

compared.difference: Existing primary is lem:timesZ, used only as support when necessary.

Existing target gives Sigma_(lambda+3) by a two-shuffle construction. New targets are a three-universal classification or the distinct cofinal-approximation Sigma_(lambda+2) construction; no direct corollary is newly counted.

editorial_notes: All ordinals are countable; lambda is a nonzero limit and delta_n is a cofinal fundamental sequence.
The summation variable in1403/1435 is read consistently with the explicitly defined delta_n fundamental sequence, and the bounded tail in1437 uses delta_n. Original source notation is preserved.

This construction is not a sum of two shuffle sums. The paper explicitly distinguishes it at1425-1426 and1520-1522 from the already prepared lambda+3 construction; its approximation-sequence and distinguished-cut argument is new work.
The public Z-power back-and-forth lemma141394 is complete support, not a newly counted target.
